chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Talhah ibn Zayd from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon them both) said:

"Whoever gives a charity (sadaqah) and it is returned to him, he should not eat it, because there is no partner for Allah, Exalted and Glorious, in anything that was designated for Him. It is merely in the status of manumission (itaqah); its return is not valid after it has freed [the debt/obligation]."
ai.seo_question: What happens to a charity if it is returned to the donor?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, emphasizing that a returned sadaqah is not merely a revocable gift but a completed transfer of ownership to God, analogous to manumission (itaqah). This highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the divine portion in charity is irrevocable, preventing the donor from reclaiming the value for personal use. The analogy to itaqah underscores the permanence of the act, distinguishing it from simple commercial transactions.
